title: Repeated-experiment suite summary
description: The suite-summary.json written over a set of repetitions of one experiment id: every attempt's observations, the medians derived from them, the paired ratios with bootstrap intervals, the dispersion beside every central value, and the gates that were checked. The per-attempt observations stay in the document so a reader can recompute every summary statistic from the same bytes that state it. Floats are allowed here because a summary is evidence, never an identity. Documentation mirror of the SuiteSummary serde type in crates/bench-schema/src/suite.rs, which is the source of truth.

experiment_id.description: The experiment every attempt below is an attempt of. This is what aggregation is keyed by; the bundle digests identify the individual attempts.

scenario_name.description: Scenario name, carried for readers who do not resolve ids.

repetitions.description: Repetitions the suite was asked for. A measurement without its repetition count is not a result.

seed.description: Seed behind every deterministic choice, including the bootstrap resampling below.

resamples.description: Bootstrap resamples behind every interval in pairs.

practical_threshold.description: The relative difference the suite was set up to care about, stated next to the intervals so that an interval excluding zero is never mistaken for a difference that matters.

attempts.description: Every attempt, valid or not, in execution order. Invalid attempts stay in the list: a median over a set nobody can reconstruct is not auditable, and what was discarded is the first thing a sceptical reader asks for.

attempt_id.description: <yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<8 hex>, which also names the bundle directory.

bundle_digest.description: Digest of the sealed bundle, so the attempt can be fetched and checked.

execution_status.description: Did the machinery do what it was told. Not validity.

run_valid.description: Does the attempt's evidence mean anything. Not execution status.

subjects.description: One entry per subject the attempt measured.

medians.description: Per-subject medians over the valid attempts, field for field with the observations above. Medians rather than means: one stalled attempt should not move the reported number.

pairs.description: Directed ratios between subjects, each naming its own denominator. A ratio with an unnamed denominator is decoration.

metric.description: Which median field the ratio is over, for example acknowledged_records_per_second.

ci_low.description: Lower end of the bootstrap interval; never above ci_high.

dispersion.description: Per-subject, per-metric spread across the repetitions. A measurement without its dispersion is not a result.

coefficient_of_variation.description: Standard deviation over the mean. Null when it could not be computed - which is a different claim from zero spread.

gates.description: Conditions the suite checked, in the order it checked them. Each carries the sentence it enforces, so a failing gate is readable without the code that ran it.

detail.description: What was actually observed, pass or fail.

claim_eligible.description: Always false in this milestone: no calibrated stable-runner thresholds and no limiting-resource classification, so no suite may support a published claim.

notes.description: Anything a reader must know that the numbers do not say.

observation.title: One subject's numbers
observation.description: The same field set for a single attempt and for the median over attempts, so that reading a median and reading the observations behind it is the same act. Every offer-to-terminal latency is in nanoseconds and is an intended_to_terminal percentile, so a subject cannot look faster by spending longer refusing to accept work. Three fields are attribution rather than comparison - declared, p99_intended_to_call_start_ns, and p99_accepted_to_terminal_ns - and they locate a difference without being able to establish one.

role.description: The subject's role in this comparison; absent when the subject list is unlabeled.

declared.description: What the adapter declared it did in the measured path, copied from kafkars.producer-benchmark.v2. On an attempt observation it is that attempt's declaration; on a median it is the declaration every valid attempt agreed on, and absent when they did not. The matched-execution-surface gate reads the per-attempt values.

p99_admission_wait_ns.description: 99th percentile of admission wait alone, reported beside the end-to-end percentiles so backpressure is visible rather than merely included.

p99_intended_to_call_start_ns.description: 99th percentile scheduler lateness. Present exactly when the load mode had a schedule to be late against; a closed-loop run reports nothing here rather than zero, because no schedule is a different statement from a schedule kept perfectly.

p99_accepted_to_terminal_ns.description: 99th percentile of the client-internal portion, terminal minus accepted. This locates a latency difference inside the client and cannot claim one: a client that refuses admission for longer looks better here by construction. Compare on p99_intended_to_terminal_ns and read this beside it. Absent only in documents written before the field existed, where a reader must treat it as unknown rather than as zero.

max_rss_bytes.description: Absent when the platform did not report it.

cpu_core_seconds.description: Absent when the platform did not report it.

cpu_core_seconds_per_million_acknowledge.description: CPU core-seconds normalized to a million acknowledged records. Total CPU is not comparable between subjects that moved different amounts of traffic; this is. Absent rather than zero when the platform reported no resources, or when nothing was acknowledged to divide by.
